- If sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 1–3% for next forecast.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices spike, model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent peak or adjust downward if sentiment turns neutral.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., sharp drop after spike), model often fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.5% per day post-spike.
- If model forecast is flat or rising slowly but true outcome shows volatility, sentiment history should trigger early adjustment — especially if sentiment shifts from neutral to bullish.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates volatility in high-sentiment periods; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast if sentiment >0.67 in last 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; forecast should be adjusted to match sentiment momentum, not just price history.
